newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. Bozell set to announce link-up soon - sources.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Bozell set to announce link-up soon - sources.

text.p: Bozell, a U.S. advertising group, is expected to announce soon a link with an advertising network of similar size, advertising and banking sources said.

They told Reuters in Cannes late on Wednesday possible partners were Havas Advertising, which is 37- percent owned by France's Havas and which said recently it was seeking an "Anglo-Saxon" partner -- and U.S.-based True North Communications.
True North owns Foote Cone & Belding ad agency network and recently finalised a "divorce" with Publicis, which severed a decade-old international cooperation agreement with the French group.

Advertising and banking executives who are attending this year's International Advertising Festival in the French resort town of Cannes told Reuters an announcement about New York-based Bozell, Jacobs, Kenyon & Eckhardt was imminent.
A banking source who works with the advertising industry said Havas Advertising and privately-owned Bozell were talking about a possible link-up.
Another source said True North "is also having close talks with Bozell".
Bozell is the world's 14th biggest advertising group.
Didier Stora, chairman of Bozell France, told Reuters he could neither confirm nor deny that his firm was in talks with Havas Advertising and True North.
He said the talk of an imminent announcement was "just another rumour".
"The health of Bozell interests lots of people," he said, adding that his group was very coveted.
"We are in contact with all the actors in the market, but there is nothing specific with any communication group," he said.
A Havas Advertising spokeswoman said various rumours about the group were circulating following comments by the company's chairman at its annual meeting last week.
Havas Advertising chairman Alain de Pouzilhac is currently in the U.S. and could not immediately be reached for comment.
De Pouzilhac last week confirmed that Havas Advertising wanted to expand beyond France and that this would ideally be achieved through an alliance with "Anglo-Saxon" agencies or networks.
The banking source told Reuters there were several good reasons for Bozell and Havas Advertising to join forces.
Bozell is well established in the U.S., is privately owned and could offer good synergy with Havas Advertising.

There would be no immediate client account conflicts between the two, experts said. Two of Bozell's big clients in Europe are Chrysler, the U.S. carmaker, and Samsung, the South Korean electronics giant.
About 36 percent of Havas Advertising's business is in France, 25 percent is in North America and 19.5 percent is in continental Europe.
Another 13 percent is in Britain, five percent is in the Asia-Pacific region and 1.5 percent is in Latin America.
Havas Advertising made 191 million frans in net attributable profit in 1996, up 26 percent from 1995.
For its part, True North no longer has the Publicis-FCB Europe advertising network, which it sold to Publicis as part of the divorce settlement.
It kept FCB agencies dotted around Europe, in Paris, London, Lisbon and Athens, as part of the agreement finalised with Publicis recently.
Publicis remains True North's main shareholder with 20 percent of its capital, while True North has 26.5 percent of Publicis Communication, itself 73.5 percent owned by Publicis SA.
Publicis chairman Maurice Levy, speaking at Publicis' annual meeting, did not rule out the French firm ultimately selling its stake in True North. DT/SLA
